newsitem.title: USA: US corp bond issuers rush to finance debt, eye FOMC.
newsitem.headline: US corp bond issuers rush to finance debt, eye FOMC.

text.p: Corporate bond primary market activity should continue at a brisk pace as U.S. corporations rush to finance debt ahead of next Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, dealers said.
"The market's on the defensive again," said one high-grade syndicate source. "I think we're going to see a rush to finance debt ahead of the Fed's next meeting."
Dealers said issuers fearing higher interest rates will mostly likely price debt now rather than risk higher financing costs later.
On Tuesday, U.S. Treasuries came under pressure after a senior Federal Reserve official told Reuters that eight of the Federal Reserve's 12 regional bank governors had requested a discount rate hike.
Market players took those comments as a signal that the FOMC committee would raise interest rates this month by 25 basis points.
Meanwhile, the market for new issues continues to build with a number of big debt offerings planned for Wednesday's business, dealers said.
"The market's doing better and I think people mainly want to get business done," another syndicate source said.
Nationsbank is expected to tap the market with $1.35 billion in a three-part debt offering as early as Wednesday, market sources said.
The first tranche consists of $500 million in five-year debt with price talk seen at 40 basis points over Treasuries.
The second tranche is for $500 million in 10-year debt with price talk seen at 65 basis points over Treasuries.
The third tranche consists of $350 million of a 20-year issue with price talk seen in the 75 basis points range.
Another $1.0 billion in five-year global debt is expected to price out of Ford Motor Credit Corp, a Ford Motor unit, sources said.
Price talk on the issue is 48 to 50 basis points over the five-year Treasury note, sources said.
Also, Daimler Benz is expected to price $500 million in 10-year debt via JP Morgan Securities, sources added.
In addition, Uruguay and Petronas are expected to issue debt in the next few week, syndicate sources said.
In Wednesday's business, Speedy Muffler King priced $125 million in B1/B-plus rated 10-year senior notes to yield 10.875 percent via Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is trading off 3/32 at 96-15/32 to yield 7.03 percent compared with 7.02 percent at Tuesday's close.
